features.name: User Registration & Login

integrations.requirement: Integrates with Security Module for authentication validation
Connects with User Role System for onboarding
Integrates with Notification System for OTP delivery
Connects with Fraud Detection System for suspicious login monitoring

features.remaining: Two-step sign-in with an authenticator app and single-use recovery codes is built, and an account that has it cannot use the API or spend on a password-only session. A sign-in from a new device notifies the owner and unusual patterns raise a risk alert. On 4 October 2026 the mfa-recover function was deployed and the API pre-request hook was confirmed installed on the hosted project; neither has been exercised there yet with a real second step or a suspended account. Phone codes cannot be sent until the Termii secrets are set. Email, SMS, OAuth and passkeys need hosted/device verification.
features.acceptance: Register with email and phone, verify/resend/expire a code, recover a password, sign in socially and with a passkey, challenge MFA, revoke a session, and review a suspicious-login event.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql sections 27 and 28). Deployed integration and user-journey acceptance are still pending.

features.name: Role-Based Onboarding

integrations.requirement: Links with Analytics System for behavior tracking

features.remaining: A new account chooses to hire or buy, work or sell, deliver, or buy for a business; each has its own set-up and its own home. Language, notification and interest preferences are saved. Which kinds of screen people open is recorded (by route shape, never whose page), with an opt-out that erases what was kept, and reported to staff by role, funnel and week-one return.
features.acceptance: Complete onboarding for every supported role, reopen saved preferences, land in the correct dashboard and prevent unauthorized role changes.
features.verification: Pending deployed integration and user-journey acceptance.

features.name: Identity Verification
features.remaining: NIN/BVN documents, selfies and CAC certificates are reviewed by staff; there is still no authoritative BVN, NIN, CAC registry, face-match or NIN-SIM check (phone OTP only proves possession of the SIM). Verification now has four tiers that set daily withdrawal limits and feed the trust score. The fraud rules do not yet use vendor or document signals. External setup deferred.
features.acceptance: Exercise each verification method, rejection and retry; validate signed vendor callbacks and evidence access/retention; apply verified tiers to trust and payments.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql section 29). Deployed integration and user-journey acceptance are still pending.

features.name: Service Listings
features.remaining: Home suggests providers from the trades someone said they came for or has booked, nearer and better reviewed first, by a fixed rule rather than a model. The video and credential workflow requires deployed storage and browser acceptance; credentials are self-reported.
features.acceptance: Create/edit a priced service, publish images/video/credentials, view as a customer, remove content, reject another provider’s file, then book and message the provider.
features.verification: Pending deployed integration and user-journey acceptance.

features.name: Job Posting & Bidding
features.remaining: Providers can revise, withdraw and re-send a quote; customers see the revision history and can only accept the version they reviewed. Posting a job with its trade and area matches it to providers by a fixed score, and the customer can invite the best fits. Budget, deadline, revision and quote-to-booking flows require staging acceptance.
features.acceptance: Post a budget and deadline; submit, amend, withdraw, compare and accept bids; verify notifications and exactly one escrow booking.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql section 24). Deployed integration and user-journey acceptance are still pending.

features.name: Booking Management
features.remaining: The staff report covers bookings created, completed, cancelled and rescheduled, their average value, and breakdowns by trade and area, with the steps from viewing a provider to booking. Multi-user rescheduling, availability conflicts and payments need hosted acceptance.
features.acceptance: Book, accept/decline, request and accept/decline a reschedule, reject conflicting slots, cancel/refund and complete/release; preserve history and notify both sides.
features.verification: Pending deployed integration and user-journey acceptance.

features.name: Live Communication System
features.remaining: A chat shows the open booking, order, purchase order and dispute between the two people, each linking to its screen. Every in-app notification can be pushed to devices with push on; sending needs the send-push function deployed with a VAPID key pair, pg_net and two settings rows, none of which is configured, and no push has reached a real device.
features.acceptance: Use two accounts to exchange text, voice and media, paginate old messages, verify unread state, deny outsiders and follow transaction-linked push deep links.
features.verification: Subscription rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql section 33); the sender's logic is unit tested. No push has been delivered to a device.

features.name: Product Management
features.remaining: A product can be sold in options (sizes, colours, packs), each with its own price and stock. Each seller has a store page. A product page suggests what the same customers also bought, more from the seller, and what is selling: counted from orders, not a model. Options have one level only and no photo per option.
features.acceptance: Create and edit a product with separately priced/stocked variants and media; discover its store, purchase, dispatch, and reconcile stock and seller settlement.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql section 31). Deployed integration and user-journey acceptance are still pending.

features.name: Shopping Cart & Checkout
features.remaining: Coupons are built: percentage or fixed amount, minimum spend, cap, end date, total and per-customer limits. A seller's coupon comes out of that seller's proceeds; a FindWork coupon applies only to FindWork's own catalog. One code per checkout. The quote the customer sees and the amount charged come from the same pricing function. A dispatched order creates a delivery for riders. The payment gateway funds the wallet rather than paying at checkout; delivery is a flat fee per seller, not priced by distance.
features.acceptance: Change cart quantities, apply valid/expired/limited coupons, manage/select private saved addresses, obtain a server quote and place multi-seller orders without overspending.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql section 31). Deployed integration and user-journey acceptance are still pending.

features.name: Order Tracking
features.remaining: The tracking page shows delivery progress, the rider and their position on a map while they carry the order, an estimated arrival, and the customer's delivery code; it refreshes every 10 seconds. Delivery updates are sent as notifications and pushed where push is on; push delivery itself is unconfigured and untested on devices.
features.acceptance: Watch status and rider location change without reloading, receive updates, and see a measured ETA with unavailable/stale-location handling.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql section 32). Deployed integration and user-journey acceptance are still pending.

features.name: Returns & Refunds
features.remaining: Manual dispute approval and wallet refunds implemented. Hosted seller-recovery, repeat settlement and physical-return operational acceptance remain.
features.acceptance: Submit evidence, approve/dismiss a return, refund before and after settlement, and prove no duplicate payout/refund or negative consumed escrow.
features.verification: Pending deployed integration and user-journey acceptance.

features.name: RFQ System
features.remaining: Quotes are compared lowest first with each supplier's verification tier and trust score. Accepting one raises a purchase order: paid into escrow at once, or held for an owner or approver when an organisation's buyer goes over its limit. A request can be limited to ID-verified suppliers or verified businesses. The supplier marks delivery, the buyer confirms to pay or puts the payment on hold for staff to decide, and silence pays the supplier after 14 days. An invoice is issued with the escrow payment. Quotes are one price for the whole request, not per line; there is no counter-offer, part delivery or part payment.
features.acceptance: Compare supplier offers, authorize approval, create a purchase obligation/invoice, fund escrow and track fulfilment.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql section 35, including fee reconciliation). Deployed integration and user-journey acceptance are still pending.

features.name: Corporate Procurement Dashboard
features.remaining: An organisation has an owner, approvers and buyers, an approval limit, and a list of approved and blocked suppliers. Its dashboard shows what was paid, what is in escrow, what awaits approval, spend by month and by supplier, and every purchase order with its printable invoice. Requests can carry up to 50 lines. Purchases are paid from the owner's wallet; the organisation has no wallet or bank account of its own. Invoices are reached through their purchase orders: there is no separate invoice list, export or tax handling. The inventory link is one-sided: a supplier can take delivered goods out of their own shop stock, but the buyer has no stock records. Platform-wide reports do not break out wholesale.
features.acceptance: A procurement team places and approves a bulk purchase, tracks supplier fulfilment/payment and retrieves historical invoices with correct access.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql section 35). Deployed integration and user-journey acceptance are still pending.

features.name: Local Marketplace Listings
features.remaining: A listing is placed in a listed area and can be found by distance from the pinned location or the device's position, within 5 to 50 km, as a list or on a map. The map is OpenStreetMap, not Google. A listing sits at its area's centre, never the seller's address, so distances are to the area, not the item. Listings posted without an area are not found by distance. New listings are scanned for copied text, off-platform payment requests and price outliers.
features.acceptance: Create rental and used-goods listings, find only those within a chosen radius, view maps, message/report sellers and manage listing lifecycle.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql section 34). Deployed integration and on-device acceptance are still pending.

features.name: Meet-Up Safety Tools
features.remaining: A buyer proposes a time and public place for a listing and the seller confirms. Either person can share their location with the other for a set time (5 minutes to 3 hours); it stops by itself and when the meet-up ends. SOS alerts FindWork staff with the person's position and who they were meeting, and works even for a suspended account; it does not contact the police, and says so beside the emergency numbers. Up to three trusted contacts can be called or texted in one tap through the phone's own apps; FindWork sends them nothing itself. Location sharing stops when the browser is closed. Staff response to an SOS has no on-call process behind it yet.
features.acceptance: Share/revoke a meetup location, expire access, trigger an SOS to authorized recipients and review an abuse report without exposing other users’ locations.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql section 34). Deployed integration and on-device acceptance are still pending.

features.name: AI Job Matching
features.remaining: A job is scored against each provider out of 100: trade 40, distance 25, budget 15, availability 10, reputation 10, and every match shows where its points came from. Customers see the best-fitting providers for a job and can invite them to quote; providers see open jobs best fit first. This is a fixed rule, not a learned model: it has not been tuned or evaluated against real outcomes, and the weights are a first proposal. Availability only checks whether the provider is taking bookings, not their calendar on the day needed. Trade is matched on the category or a mention of it, not on an analysis of the description.
features.acceptance: Rank real providers by skills, location, budget and availability; explain recommendations and evaluate quality against fixed fixtures.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql section 38). Not evaluated for match quality.

features.name: AI Fraud Detection
features.remaining: These are fixed, explainable rules, not a trained model: new or shared devices, top-up-then-withdraw, rapid or large money movements, repeat refunds, copied listings, listings that take the deal off the platform, price outliers, message bursts and repeated reports or disputes. Each raises an alert for a person to review; none acts on its own. Thresholds are first guesses and need tuning against real activity. No machine-learning or AI scoring, and no device fingerprint beyond a browser-held id and IP address.
features.acceptance: Capture consent-appropriate risk signals, flag seeded fraud cases, explain decisions and support human review/appeal without silently moving money.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql sections 27 and 29). Deployed integration and user-journey acceptance are still pending.

features.name: AI Voice Assistant
features.remaining: A microphone button on Home takes a spoken or typed request and opens the right screen; a new account can choose its role by voice. Common requests in English and Pidgin are understood on the device with no service at all. Everything else, and Yoruba, Igbo and Hausa, goes to the assistant function, which calls Claude. The same function answers support questions from FindWork's own rules, translates chat messages, and helps with lessons. On 4 October 2026 it was deployed with an API key and answered live requests: a Yoruba command, a Pidgin command, a support question and a translation into Hausa. Lesson help and staff dispute summaries have not been run live, and no native speaker has reviewed the Yoruba, Igbo or Hausa. Speech uses the browser's own engines: it is absent in Firefox, and whether a browser can hear Yoruba, Igbo or Hausa has not been tested. The app's own text is English only.
features.acceptance: Complete onboarding/navigation in agreed languages by voice and text, handle failed recognition, request confirmation for consequential actions and hand off to support.
features.verification: Command parsing, prompts and answer handling are unit tested; metering executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql section 39). Four live requests succeeded on the hosted project the same day. Speech has not been tried on devices.

features.name: Wallet System
features.remaining: Wallet-to-wallet transfers are built: the recipient is found by exact phone number or email, a retry cannot send twice, and daily limits follow the verification tier. Deposits use Paystack; withdrawals are still sent by hand. Bank account validation, automatic payouts and reconciliation are deferred with external setup.
features.acceptance: Deposit with callback/replay protection, transfer to a confirmed recipient once, withdraw with failure recovery, and reconcile balances/history.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql section 30). Deployed integration and user-journey acceptance are still pending.

features.name: Escrow Payments
features.remaining: Bookings, seller orders and wholesale purchase orders are all held in escrow. A quoted job can be paid in two to six stages: the full price is held at acceptance, the customer releases each stage in order, and cancelling refunds only what was not released. A seller with an open high-risk alert is not paid automatically. Hosted concurrency acceptance remains.
features.acceptance: Hold/release/refund funds for each transaction family; lock disputes; reject concurrent/repeated settlement and reconcile customer, seller and fees.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql sections 29 and 30, including reconciliation of reported fees after staged releases). Deployed integration and user-journey acceptance are still pending.

features.name: Subscription Billing
features.remaining: An in-app reminder is sent once, three days before each paid renewal; it also arrives as a push on devices that have push switched on, but not by email or SMS. The reminder and renewal schedules were confirmed active on the hosted project on 4 October 2026. Insufficient-funds behavior and premium entitlements need validation. Gateway is indirect through wallet.
features.acceptance: Subscribe/change plan once, send a reminder before renewal, renew or downgrade on insufficient funds and verify billing history/actual entitlements.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql section 23). Deployed integration and user-journey acceptance are still pending.

features.name: Rider Management
features.remaining: Riders apply, staff approve them, and an approved rider goes online, takes or is assigned deliveries, reports their position, hands over against the customer's delivery code and is paid 80% of the delivery fee into their wallet. A delivery is created when an order is dispatched. Rider ID is checked by staff at approval, not enforced by the database. The 80% share is a first proposal. No rider ratings, shifts, zones, batching rules or cash-on-delivery; riders work in the browser, not a native app, so location stops when the screen is closed.
features.acceptance: Onboard a rider, accept an assignment, update availability and location, prove delivery and reconcile rider earnings.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql section 32). Deployed integration, real devices and user-journey acceptance are still pending.

features.name: Route Optimization
features.remaining: A rider with several orders is shown the shortest order of stops (each collected before it is delivered) and a link that opens the round in Google Maps. This uses straight-line distance, not the road network. Arrival times are estimated from distance, vehicle and time of day in Lagos; that is a fixed congestion pattern, not live traffic. The route-estimate function replaces the estimate with a routed, traffic-aware time from Google's Routes API; it is deployed, but has no maps key and has not been run against the real service.
features.acceptance: Route assigned deliveries using traffic-aware travel time, refresh ETA, handle provider failures and prevent exposure outside the active delivery.
features.verification: Stop ordering and the routing function's logic are unit tested; arrival estimates executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026. Google Routes has not been called. Deployed and on-road acceptance pending.

features.name: Stories & Reels
features.remaining: Sellers post stories (a photo or video, gone after a day) and reels (video that stays), optionally tagged with one of their products. A feed shows them newest first; each links to the seller's store and the tagged product, and appears on the store page. Unique views and likes are counted per post. Posts can be reported and removed by moderators. Videos are stored and played as uploaded: no transcoding, thumbnails, captions or music. There are no comments, shares, follows-only feed or ranking, and uploads are capped at 50 MB.
features.acceptance: Publish/view/report short videos and expiring stories, track engagement and follow real store/product links.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql section 37). Upload and playback have not been tried against hosted storage or on phones.

features.name: Livestream Selling
features.remaining: FindWork provides the selling room around a stream: a paced live chat the seller can moderate, the products on sale with one pinned on screen, add-to-cart and wallet checkout, a viewer count, and a notification to everyone who saved the seller when they go live. It does not carry the video. The seller broadcasts with their own tool and pastes the watch link; YouTube and direct video links play inside the app, others open in a new tab. Capturing and distributing video from the phone inside FindWork needs a streaming provider, which is deferred. Chat refreshes every three seconds rather than instantly.
features.acceptance: Start/join/end a stream, moderate chat, tag available products and complete checkout; handle ended streams and restricted hosts.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql section 37). No real stream has been run.

features.name: Online Courses
features.remaining: Content staff can now write courses: lessons with text, an uploaded video or a link to one, and a quiz with a pass mark. Lesson material and quiz answers are readable only as intended (the enrolled; never the answers). A lesson with nothing in it cannot be completed. Passing the quiz, or finishing a course that has none, issues a certificate with a code anyone can verify without an account, shown on the holder's profile. The seeded courses still have no real lesson content: someone has to write it. No AI learning assistant, no instructor accounts outside staff, no video transcoding or captions.
features.acceptance: Enroll without duplicate charge, consume real text/video lessons, pass server-validated quizzes, issue/verify a certificate and use grounded learning help.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql sections 7 and 36). Video upload and playback have not been tried against hosted storage.

features.name: Internship Matching
features.remaining: Internships are their own listings, posted by ID-verified accounts, with skills, stipend, length and a closing date. An applicant sends a note once; the employer sees applicants best match first and shortlists, accepts or declines; both are notified. The match is the share of the listed skills the person has (from their stated skills, certificates and trade) plus a little for being in the same area: a fixed rule, not a learned model. The old internship entries in the course catalogue are no longer shown. No interview scheduling or offer letters.
features.acceptance: Publish an internship, match skills, submit an application, review/change its status and notify the applicant.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql section 36). Deployed integration and user-journey acceptance are still pending.

features.name: Trust Score System
features.remaining: A composite score out of 100 (verification 30, reputation 30, history 20, conduct 20) is stored per account, refreshed when its inputs change, shown on provider profiles and classifieds, and broken down for the owner. The weights are a first proposal and need agreeing; the score is not yet shown on products, chat or job quotes.
features.acceptance: Explain a reproducible trust score from verified signals, transaction and complaint outcomes; prevent self-written scores and expose appropriate history.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql section 29). Deployed integration and user-journey acceptance are still pending.

features.name: Transaction Monitoring
features.remaining: Every ledger entry is scanned as it is written and rule matches go to the staff risk queue, where they are reviewed or dismissed with a note. Rule thresholds need tuning; there is no case management beyond the alert, and no regulatory reporting.
features.acceptance: Scan known suspicious transactions, explain/triage alerts, restrict when authorized and preserve review history.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql section 29). Deployed integration and user-journey acceptance are still pending.

features.name: Dispute Management
features.remaining: Both participants and moderators can respond on a case with explicitly shared photo evidence. Staff can ask for an AI summary of a case: what happened, what is agreed and contested, what is missing and what to ask. It is told not to recommend an outcome, and the decision stays with the member of staff; it needs the assistant function and an API key, and has not been run against the real API. Reports, listings and messages are also screened by fixed rules that raise alerts. Wholesale purchase orders use a simpler hold-and-decide path rather than full disputes.
features.acceptance: Submit evidence, let both sides respond, review evidence as admin, freeze escrow, resolve once and audit decisions; AI triage must retain human settlement authority.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql section 25). Deployed integration and user-journey acceptance are still pending.

features.name: User Management
features.remaining: Staff can look up an account, see its devices, security events, disputes, reports and alerts, suspend or reinstate it with a reason, and admins can assign staff roles (admin, moderator, finance, support) that limit which parts of the console and which operator functions each can use. Suspension blocks spending, new bookings, orders, quotes, listings and messages and hides the account's listings; the API hook that blocks every other write must be confirmed on the hosted project. No link to behaviour analytics yet.
features.acceptance: Locate users, inspect activity, suspend across APIs and storage, manage permitted roles without escalation, review verification and audit actions.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql section 27). Deployed integration and user-journey acceptance are still pending.

features.name: Platform Analytics
features.remaining: Staff reports now cover income and obligations from the ledger; people by role, week-one return and verified share; visits, screens opened and the steps to booking and ordering; bookings by trade and area; top sellers, coupon discounts, wholesale and rider payouts; with CSV export of the daily figures. The projection of the next week is a straight-line trend adjusted for weekday, clearly labelled as arithmetic and not a model; there is no AI. Engagement only covers people who have not opted out, and only since tracking began. Delivery charges, gateway costs and taxes are outside the income figures.
features.acceptance: Reconcile reports to ledger/bookings/orders with defined revenue and escrow semantics; filter/export accurate aggregates under admin authorization.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql sections 26, 30, 35 and 38). Deployed integration and user-journey acceptance are still pending.

features.name: Real-Time Analytics
features.remaining: The staff report refreshes on its own (30 seconds for money, 60 for engagement) and shows when it was calculated; it polls rather than streams. Staff can look up one account's visits and screens over 30 days. Flagged transactions appear in the risk queue as they happen. There is no AI analytics engine.
features.acceptance: Capture activity, show time-filtered live metrics with freshness and access boundaries, and validate predictive outputs against historical data.
features.verification: Database rules executed on plain Postgres 17 on 4 October 2026 (supabase/checks/business_rules.sql section 26). Deployed integration and user-journey acceptance are still pending.
